svg.title: Joseph Smith and Mormonism vs. Karl Marx and Marxism, 1805 to today
svg.text: Mormonism and Marxism side by side, 1805 to today: two founders, two movements, two answers on property and equality

Joseph Smith and Karl Marx, the movements that grew from them, and their teachings on property and religion, on one linear
axis from 1805 to today. Bands are equal in importance; bar thickness implies no measure. Ages are computed from birth
dates. LDS leader statements on communism shown: 1917, 1936, 1942, 1961, 1963.
LABELLED PERSPECTIVE · NOT THIS MAP’S CONCLUSION
Some Latter-day Saints read the near-simultaneous rise of the Church (1830) and Marxism (1848) as spiritual opposition: President David O. McKay said in
1951–52 “we are facing Satan himself” of Communists. Historians point instead to shared context: revivals, industrialization, 1837 and 1848 crises, and
many communal experiments of the era.
